title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Enteral medication via feeding tube
decisions.scenario: A nurse prepares to administer medication through a patient’s feeding tube. The medication has been crushed, but the nurse has not yet verified whether the medication is suitable for crushing.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Verify medication compatibility with tube administration.

decisions.title: Look-alike sound-alike drugs
decisions.scenario: While preparing medications, a nurse notices two different medications with very similar names stored next to each other in the medication cupboard.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Transdermal patch safety
decisions.scenario: During a routine assessment, a nurse notices that a patient has more than one fentanyl transdermal patch applied to the skin. The patient appears drowsy and is breathing more slowly than usual.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Remove excess patches and notify provider.

decisions.title: Antibiotic stewardship
decisions.scenario: A patient presents with symptoms of a viral respiratory infection and requests antibiotics, stating that antibiotics have helped them feel better in the past.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Educate patient about appropriate antibiotic use.

decisions.title: Medication reconciliation
decisions.scenario: A patient is admitted to the ward from the emergency department. The medication history is incomplete, and the patient is unsure about the names and doses of home medications.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: IV infiltration
decisions.scenario: A patient receiving IV medication reports increasing pain at the IV insertion site. On inspection, the site appears swollen and cool to touch.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Stop the infusion and assess the site.

decisions.title: Rapid-acting antihypertensive
decisions.scenario: A patient receiving IV antihypertensive medication experiences a sudden and significant drop in blood pressure shortly after the infusion begins. The patient reports feeling lightheaded.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Slow or stop infusion and monitor closely.

decisions.title: Medication storage error
decisions.scenario: During a routine medication check, a nurse finds a medication that requires refrigeration stored at room temperature for an unknown period.
